**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The MINCOMMIT rule is satisfied at the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback:

- **§ 2.1 (p0013)** — the operative clause: *"No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall."* This is a direct match to the preferred position (fees for usage/ordered services only), and the final limb pre-empts any argument that non-renewal creates a shortfall claim.
- **§ 7.1 (p0026)** — backstops it by barring Vendor from imposing "platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge" not identified in the Order Form, closing the back-door minimum-fee route.
- **§ 12.3 (p0051)** — confirms Customer has made no "exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."
- **§ 8.2 / 8.3** — even if an Order Form did carry a commitment, Customer can opt out of renewal on 30 days' notice (with a reminder mechanic extending the deadline), and uplifts are capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. No multi-year take-or-pay exposure.

Two items reviewed and deliberately not flagged under this rule:
- The "shortfall" language in **§ 22 (p0095–p0096)** is an audit true-up of under-reported usage quantities, not a take-or-pay penalty — expressly the true-up mechanic the playbook prefers.
- **§ 7.7 (p0032)** imposes punitive liquidated damages of 15% of annual Fees per week on late payment. That is a genuine customer-adverse term, but it is a payment/late-fee issue, not a minimum purchase commitment or volume restriction — it belongs to the payment-terms rule and should not be double-flagged here.
